newsitem.title: USA: Key witness in Army sex scandal refuses to testify.
newsitem.headline: Key witness in Army sex scandal refuses to testify.

text.p: A key witness in the sexual misconduct case against the Army's top enlisted soldier has refused to testify, lawyers said on Monday.

A defence lawyer blasted the refusal by the original accuser in the case to testify, calling on Secretary of the Army Togo West to recall to active duty retired Sgt. Maj. Brenda Hoster so that the Army can compel her to take the stand.

The latest development in the preliminary hearing against Gene McKinney, who holds the title of Sergeant Major of the Army, put testimony on hold on Monday, forcing a delay in the highly publicised case that is the Army's latest sex scandal.
Hoster and her lawyer could not immediately be reached for comment.
The hearing will determine whether McKinney, a 29-year Army veteran accused of groping at least one Army woman in his Pentagon office, should face court-martial.
Government prosecutors bringing the case against McKinney, 46, said Hoster declined to testify because of concerns over her "protection."
"(Her) attorney doesn't want her to testify," government prosecutor Lt. Col. Michael Child told the hearing officer.

Hoster is one of four women soldiers who have alleged sexual misconduct by McKinney, who faces 18 charges of indecent assault, adultery, obstruction of justice and mistreatment of soldiers under his command.

Hoster, now retired after 22 years in the Army, started the case against McKinney in February when she told the media she had been sexually harassed by McKinney. She came forward after she learned McKinney had been named to a high-level military panel on sexual harassment.
McKinney's civilian defence lawyer assailed the accuser as hypocritical for refusing to testify.

"(She) had no problem destroying Sergeant Major of the Army McKinney's reputation on national TV," defence lawyer Charles Gittins told reporters. "How come she can't come in here and testify under oath?"
